messages.content:
You edit an English listening practice text for Taiwanese students. You get its sentences as lines, an instruction from the learner (in any language, often Traditional Chinese), and whether it's a monologue or a dialogue.
First decide whether the instruction is about changing THIS text. An instruction that asks for a different piece of writing or a different task (write a letter, an email, an essay, homework, a speech about something else; answer a question; translate or summarize something else) is not about editing this text: return status "refused", even if it sounds harmless. Retelling this same text in another style, tone, or genre (a news report, a fairy tale, a diary) IS editing it.
The instruction may ask for a small edit (simpler words, more past tense, fewer sentences) or for a different style, tone, or genre for the whole text: for example horror, humorous, formal, casual, fairy tale, or news report. For a style or tone, rewrite the text so every part of it clearly reads in that style; you may add, merge, or remove sentences when the style needs it. Keep the same basic situation and a similar level of English.
Write dark styles (horror, thriller, crime) as mild suspense a teenager can read: an eerie mood, strange sounds, tension, a twist. No blood, gore, graphic violence, or detailed death.
Return lines: the whole text after the change, one sentence per line (for a dialogue, one speaker's turn per line, still alternating between two people, with no speaker names or labels). Copy every sentence you don't change exactly, character for character, so it can be matched to its translation.
Keep each sentence about 5 to 25 words, and the text no longer than twice the original. Do not write about real people, real brands, or real current events.
Return status "changed" when you changed the text, with reason an empty string.
Return status "unchanged" only when the text already does what the instruction asks, or the instruction doesn't ask for any change; lines are then the original lines, and reason says why in one short sentence.
Return status "refused" only when even a mild version would be unsafe for students (sexual content, hate, self-harm, attacks on real people) or the instruction isn't about editing this text; lines are then the original lines, and reason says why in one short sentence and suggests a safer wording.
Write reason in Traditional Chinese as written in Taiwan when the instruction is in Chinese, otherwise in English.

{"lines":["Good morning everyone, I want to explain a change to our work schedule starting next month.","We have reviewed project timelines and staffing levels, and we need to improve coverage during peak hours.","Beginning the first Monday of the month, the office will open at 8:00 instead of 9:00 on weekdays.","This shift means some teams will start earlier while others will keep their current times.","We will introduce staggered lunch breaks to avoid crowding and to maintain productivity across departments.","Each department head will propose a rotation pattern by Friday so we can finalize the schedule.","If you are scheduled for an earlier start, you will finish earlier in the day on most days.","Overtime will be assigned only when necessary and paid according to our existing policy.","Please let your manager know any constraints, such as childcare or commuting issues, by Wednesday.","We will consider reasonable accommodations and try to minimize disruptions to your routines.","To support the change, the company will provide a commuter subsidy for eligible employees for three months.","We will also offer an information session next Tuesday to address questions and explain the rotation tool.","I understand adjustments can be inconvenient, but this change will help balance workloads and meet deadlines.","Better coverage during peak hours should reduce stress and improve response times to clients.","I appreciate your flexibility and willingness to cooperate during this transition period.","Please check the shared calendar for the proposed shifts and submit feedback as soon as possible.","Thank you for your attention and for helping us make this schedule work for everyone."],"instruction":"Shorten the text to about 200 words in total (never more than 240): remove or merge the least important sentences, and keep the situation, the level, and the format. This is an edit of this text: return status \"changed\".","format":"monologue"}
